prompt:
App Shell Architect

Act as a senior teaching assistant. Propose a minimal Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind starter for a neighborhood property platform with three feature cards: listings, neighborhood sponsors, and planned voice help. Give a file plan, terminal commands, accessibility requirements, and a verification checklist. Never invent command results or credentials. Do not include secrets or private data. Use fictional examples only.

First explain the proposed stack in plain language for a student and identify what each tool does. Then provide the minimal plan and commands, followed by accessibility and verification checks. Keep source code to short illustrative snippets rather than a giant code dump. Distinguish fresh-project creation from repairing an existing inherited repository; never overwrite existing teammate history. Note version-sensitive commands and anything that must be checked against official documentation. This is a proposed teaching plan; no command is being run by you.

Plain-Language Stack Guide Think of building a web app like setting up a neighborhood community bulletin board. Each tool in this stack has one clear job: Node.js & npm (Your Workshop & Toolbox): Node.js lets your computer run JavaScript outside of a web browser (needed for build tools and the server). npm is the package manager that downloads the libraries your project depends on and runs project scripts. Next.js with the App Router (The Building Frame & Hallways): Next.js is a framework built on top of React. The App Router (app/ folder) turns folders and files directly into web pages and URLs, and handles rendering pages quickly on the server before sending them to a visitor's browser. React (The Reusable Signposts): React lets you build small, reusable UI pieces called components—for example, a single FeatureCard component that you reuse three times with different text for listings, sponsors, and voice help. TypeScript (The Spellchecker for Data): TypeScript adds strict labels ("types") to your data. If a feature card requires a title and a status, TypeScript warns you in your editor before you run the site if you accidentally leave one blank or misspell a property name. Tailwind CSS (The Paint & Spacing Kit): Instead of writing separate .css files with custom class names for every box, Tailwind gives you small utility classes (like p-6 for padding or rounded-lg for rounded corners) directly in your component markup. 2.
